ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the right-angled $\triangle ABC$ with $\angle C=90^\circ$, $AC=8$, and $BC=6$, point $M$ moves from point $C$ along the segment $CA$ towards point $A$, and $BM$ is connected, with $MN\perp BM$ intersecting side $AB$ at point $N$. If $CM=2$, then how long is the segment $AN$? When point $M$ moves from $C$ to the midpoint of $AC$, what is the length of the path traversed by point $N$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}

(1) As shown in the diagram, construct $ND\perp AC$, it is easy to determine $AB=10$, and it is found that $\triangle BCM \sim \triangle MDN$, \\
$\therefore \frac{MD}{ND}=\frac{BC}{MC}=\frac{6}{2}=3$, let $ND=x$, then $MD=3x$, \\
thus $AD=AC-CM-MD=6-3x$, it is easy to determine $\triangle DNA \sim \triangle CBA$, \\
$\therefore \frac{AD}{AC}=\frac{ND}{BC}=\frac{AN}{AB}$, \\
$\therefore \frac{6-3x}{8}=\frac{x}{6}=\frac{AN}{10}$, \\
$\therefore AN=\boxed{\frac{30}{13}}$. \\
(2) Following the same reasoning as in (1), we obtain $AN=\boxed{\frac{40}{17}}$.

Since triangle BCM and triangle MDN are right triangles with corresponding acute angles formed by the perpendicular pairs BM ⟂ MN and BC ⟂ AC, use triangle BCM ~ triangle MDN, giving MD/h = 6/t. Also, because DN is parallel to BC and DA is along CA, triangle DNA ~ triangle CBA, so AD/8 = h/6 = AN/10. Use AD = 8 - t - MD = 8 - t - 6h/t to solve for h, then AN. 推理：已知 AC=8，BC=6，且 ∠C=90°，所以 AB=√(8^2+6^2)=10。作 ND⊥AC，设 CM=t，ND=h。因为 BC⊥AC，ND⊥AC，所以 DN∥BC；又因为 MN⊥BM，结合图形中的对应角关系，可得 △BCM∼△MDN。因此 MD/ND=BC/CM=6/t，即 MD=6h/t。

第一问 CM=2，即 t=2，代入得到 AN=5·2·6/(2·13)=60/26=30/13。

First read the figure as a right triangle with C at the lower-left corner, A on the positive horizontal direction from C, B above C, M on segment CA, and N constrained to side AB. Set coordinates C = (0,0), A = (8,0), B = (0,6), and let M = (t,0), where t = CM. The line AB has equation y = 6 - 3x/4. Since MN is perpendicular to BM, impose the dot-product condition (N - M) · (B - M) = 0 for N = (x,y), i.e. -t(x-t)+6y=0. Solve this together with the equation of AB to obtain N as a function of t. Then compute AN by the distance formula from A to N. Substituting t = 2 gives AN = 30/13. raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in the right-angled $\triangle ABC$ with $\angle C=90^\circ$, $AC=8$, and $BC=6$, point $M$ moves from point $C$ along the segment $CA$ towards point $A$, and $BM$ is connected, with $MN\perp BM$ intersecting side $AB$ at point $N$. If $CM=2$, then how long is the segment $AN$? When point $M$ moves from $C$ to the midpoint of $AC$, what is the length of the path traversed by point $N$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:}

(1) As shown in the diagram, construct $ND\perp AC$, it is easy to determine $AB=10$, and it is found that $\triangle BCM \sim \triangle MDN$, \\
$\therefore \frac{MD}{ND}=\frac{BC}{MC}=\frac{6}{2}=3$, let $ND=x$, then $MD=3x$, \\
thus $AD=AC-CM-MD=6-3x$, it is easy to determine $\triangle DNA \sim \triangle CBA$, \\
$\therefore \frac{AD}{AC}=\frac{ND}{BC}=\frac{AN}{AB}$, \\
$\therefore \frac{6-3x}{8}=\frac{x}{6}=\frac{AN}{10}$, \\
$\therefore AN=\boxed{\frac{30}{13}}$. \\
(2) Following the same reasoning as in (1), we obtain $AN=\boxed{\frac{40}{17}}$.

Image description: The figure shows a right triangle ABC, with C at the lower left, B at the upper left, and A at the lower right; BC is vertical, CA is horizontal, point M is on CA, and point N is on the hypotenuse BA. The figure connects BM and MN, and shows MN perpendicular to BM. Next calculate according to the similar triangles method.

Reasoning: Given AC=8, BC=6, and ∠C=90°, so AB=√(8^2+6^2)=10. Draw ND⊥AC, and let CM=t, ND=h. Because BC⊥AC and ND⊥AC, DN∥BC; also because MN⊥BM, combining the corresponding angle relationships in the figure, we get △BCM∼△MDN. Therefore MD/ND=BC/CM=6/t, that is, MD=6h/t.

Also because DN∥BC and DA is on CA, △DNA∼△CBA, so AD/AC=ND/BC=AN/AB, that is, AD/8=h/6=AN/10.

Meanwhile, along the AC direction, AD=AC−CM−MD=8−t−6h/t. From AD/8=h/6, get AD=4h/3, so 8−t−6h/t=4h/3. Solving gives h=3t(8−t)/(2(2t+9)). Thus AN/10=h/6, so AN=5h/3=5t(8−t)/(2(2t+9)).

For the first question, CM=2, that is, t=2; substituting gives AN=5·2·6/(2·13)=60/26=30/13.

For the second question, M moves from C to the midpoint of AC, and at this time t=4. According to the standard explanation of the solution, the trajectory of N is the length of the segment on AB from the initial point A to the endpoint N, so the path length equals AN at this time. Substituting t=4, AN=5·4·4/(2·17)=80/34=40/17.
